title: RAG Architecture Overview
description: Map the end-to-end RAG pipeline from document ingestion to grounded LLM response, and identify failure modes at each stage.

blocks.text: A production RAG pipeline usually has five stages: ingest, chunk, embed, store, retrieve, and generate. Each stage affects latency, cost, and answer quality. Weakness in any stage can degrade the final result.

blocks.title: Typical flow in a .NET backend
items: **Ingest** — read documents from files, databases, or APIs.
**Chunk** — split documents into passages small enough for the model and retrieval system.
**Embed** — convert chunks to vectors with an embedding model.
**Store** — persist vectors with metadata in a vector-capable store.
**Retrieve** — find the most relevant chunks for a user query.
**Generate** — compose a prompt from system rules, retrieved context, and user input, then call the LLM.

blocks.title: End-to-end RAG pipeline sketch
blocks.content: A complete C# service that demonstrates ingest, chunk, embed, store, retrieve, and generate.

blocks.title: Common problems in RAG systems
items: **Bad chunking** — chunks cut important context in half, hurting comprehension.
**Wrong embedding model** — a model trained on short web text may struggle with long technical documents.
**Weak retrieval** — top-k returns irrelevant passages and pollutes the prompt.
**Prompt overflow** — too much retrieved text exhausts the context window.
**No citations** — users cannot verify where the answer came from.

blocks.title: Start from the user's question
blocks.text: Do not optimize retrieval in isolation. Measure end-to-end answer quality with questions your users actually ask.

data.caption: High-level RAG pipeline in a .NET backend
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    A[Ingest documents] --> B[Chunk text]
    B --> C[Generate embeddings]
    C --> D[Store vectors + metadata]
    D --> E[Retrieve top chunks]
    E --> F[Compose prompt]
    F --> G[LLM generates answer]
    G --> H[Return answer + citations]

items.question: Should I build RAG from scratch?
items.answer: Start with a library like Semantic Kernel or LlamaIndex to avoid rewriting ingestion, chunking, and retrieval logic. Move to custom code only when you need specialized behavior.

items.question: Where does C# fit in RAG?
items.answer: C# is ideal for the orchestration layer: ingestion, chunking, retrieval, API endpoints, and integration with existing .NET systems.

items.question: Is async important for RAG?
items.answer: Yes. Embedding, retrieval, and LLM calls are I/O-heavy. Use async C# throughout to keep your backend scalable.

blocks.title: Draw Your First Pipeline
blocks.description: Sketch the RAG pipeline for a concrete dataset before writing any code.
steps: Choose a document collection you care about.
Identify chunk boundaries and chunk size.
List the metadata you would attach to each chunk.
Write the user questions you expect to ask.
blocks.expectedOutcome: You should have a concrete pipeline diagram and a list of design choices to test later with code.
